note: Reusable conversations by occupation (placeholder authored text, owner review pending). Facts are read from the simulation by narrative/occupations.py; a line only appears when its facts hold, so nothing claims what the world does not contain. Added 18 Oct 2026: `tribes` (intro_home, intro_away, hub, often and topics per tribe: barbarians, empire, frisians, atlanteans, amazons; facts this_village, home_village, is_home, home_distance, trade, tribe, gate_distance, gate_compass).

lumberjack.label: Lumberjack
intro: {name}, lumberjack. I fell the old trees and the carriers haul the logs away.
Mind the axe. I am {name}; I cut timber for the {faction} settlement.
hub: Make it quick, there is a tree waiting.

topics.text: What does a lumberjack do all day?
lines: I walk out to a tree that has stood long enough, fell it, carry the log back and start again.
A {carrying}, as you see. It goes to {workplace}.

topics.text: How is the forest around here?
lines: Plenty of tall trees within a short walk: {trees_big} of them near me right now.

topics.text: How is the forest around here?
lines: The big trees close to the hut are getting few, {trees_big} within a short walk. I go further each time.
{saplings} saplings and poles close by. I leave those alone, mostly.

topics.text: Is there timber in the store?
lines: {logs} logs in the warehouses of the {faction} settlement. The sawmill and the builders will want every one of them.

topics.text: Is there timber in the store?
lines: Not one log, the last I looked. That is why I am out here.
Soldiers of another colour have been seen close by. I keep my axe near.

ranger.label: Forester
intro: {name}, forester. I plant saplings and watch them grow.
I am {name}. Somebody has to see that there are trees for next year.
hub: Careful where you step, there are seedlings.
What would you like to know?

lines: I find open ground, dig a hole and plant a sapling. Then I do it again. The trees do the rest, slowly.
{saplings} saplings and poles within sight of me. Every one of them is a log in some future year.
Hardly any yet. It takes a long time for a seedling to become a log.

topics.text: Does the settlement need more timber?
lines: It always does. But a forest cut faster than it grows is a forest that ends.

topics.text: Do you work with the lumberjack?
lines: We share the same trees, though not always the same idea of how fast they should become logs.

stonemason.label: Stonemason
intro: {name}, stonemason. I cut stone from the rocks by the quarry.
I am {name}. If it is hard and grey, I probably cut it.
hub: Watch your feet, there is stone dust.

lines: I chip granite from the rock near the quarry and carry it back to be stored. Slow work, but stone does not rot.
{rocks} rock formations still stand around me. Plenty of work yet.
For building, mostly. Every wall and every foundation starts as somebody's rock.

hunter.label: Hunter
intro: {name}, hunter. I follow the game and bring meat home.
I am {name}. Quiet feet and patient eyes, that is the whole trade.

lines: Whatever the woods give: deer, mostly. I track it, shoot it and carry it back.
{animals} animals within sight of me this morning.
Nothing in sight at the moment. The animals know when someone is looking for them.

carrier.label: Carrier
intro: {name}. I carry wares along this road, one load at a time.
I am {name}, a carrier. Nobody notices the road until it stops.
hub: Yes? I have somewhere to be.

lines: Whatever the buildings hand me: logs, stone, and what the settlement needs next. I walk my stretch of road and hand it on.

topics.text: What is that you are carrying?
lines: A {carrying}. It is going where the road leads.
Nothing just now. I walk back and forth until someone has something for me.

soldier.label: Soldier
intro: {name}. I am one of the {faction} soldiers.
I am {name}, a soldier of the {faction} settlement.

lines: I stand ready. If strangers come, I am the one who goes out to meet them.
{soldiers} of us stand with the {faction} settlement. It is not many.
No barracks yet. We are few and the settlement is small.
We have {barracks}, yes. It is where soldiers are made.
Soldiers of another colour have been seen near here. We are watching.
Quiet, so far. I do not trust the quiet, but I will take it.

worker.label: Worker
intro: I am {name}. {workplace}, if you are looking for me.

lines: I keep {workplace} running for the {faction} settlement.
It grows a little every day. That is all I can say for sure.

shared_topics.text: You are looking at me strangely.

lines.text: Put that down. I mean the staff. I saw what you did on the road and so did half the settlement, and I would like to finish my work with my skin on.

lines: People say an apprentice set a carrier alight. People say it was you. I am not asking; I am telling you what people say, so you know what the silence is when you walk past.
Smoke. Trees. The lumberjack is not pleased; he says somebody has been doing his work for him, badly, and leaving nothing to carry.
For you, maybe. I have walked this road eleven times since you last did anything that I could see. I am not judging. I am counting; it is a habit of the trade.

lines.text: The best of us. They never asked for thanks, which is why nobody thinks to give it.
Keeps to themselves. Clever, I suppose, but clever is not the same as caring.
Fair, and a little distant. I would not say a bad word of them.
They taught half the settlement their letters, and never raised a hand to anyone.
Stubborn as a root. Which is not a complaint.

shared_topics.text: What do you make of wizards, in general?

lines.text: Somebody should be in charge who can actually do things. It might as well be them.
Wizards, kings, headmen. Same disease, different hats.
A gift is a trust. They answer to something above themselves, or they should.
Fine, so long as they pay for what they break. Everyone does.
The land has its own ways. A wizard who forgets that will find out. Gently or not.
Useful, if they keep to their duty. Dangerous otherwise. Same as a sword.
Have you noticed they all talk in threes? Three colours, three places. As if somebody had written it.

shared_topics.text: Does it bother you, having an apprentice wizard about the place?

lines.text: Bother me? It makes me prouder of the village, if you want the truth.
Not at all. Folk like you remind us to be better than we are.
As long as you stay out of my way and mind the timber, no.
A little. You are young. Young and powerful is a thing worth watching.
I would rather you did not stand near my work, if it is the same to you.

shared_topics.text: I heard you had some trouble in the forest.
lines: You settled it, or tried. That counts for more than most. If you ever want a favour, ask.

lines.text: A man in a black travelling cloak came up the east road last week asking after {mentor} by name. Polite. Too polite. I did not like it.
Carriers say there is a stranger on the roads with light under his cloak, asking after old teachers. Carriers say a lot of things.

lines: And the usual: the Trial gate, {gate_distance} tiles {gate_compass} of here, opens again this season, and the road is full of fools walking towards it.

shared_topics.text: Does anyone keep count of all this?

lines.text: Somebody does. Not me. I get asked the same four things by every apprentice with a staff, I answer them, and the hills do not change. If you find out who is counting, tell them I would like a day off.

often: I am beginning to think you have nowhere to be.
If you are counting us, I am the same one as before.
Yes. Still me. Still working. What is it this time?

barbarians.note: The home tribe on the default world: blunt, warm, axes and ale. Red and Orange.
intro_home: {name}. {trade}, and a neighbour of your mother's, so mind your manners. What is it?
Ha, the apprentice. {name}, {trade}. Your mother said you would come round asking things. Ask.
intro_away: {name}, {trade} of {this_village}. You are the one from {home_village} with the staff; the carriers said you were walking this way. Well. Here you are.
A stranger with a staff. {name}, {trade}. We do not get many from {home_village} out here. Speak up.
hub: Make it quick, the axe does not swing itself.
often: You again. The others have started a count.
If you have nothing to do, there is always wood.

lines.text: {this_village}? Timber, stone, meat, and more opinions than houses. Everyone here would die for the next person along and tell them so to their face.
{this_village} is a {trade}'s village like any other: we cut, we carry, we drink what is left. You will find no wizards here, which is why we are so calm.

lines: That a stranger walked into it and killed an old wizard in the square, and that the apprentice was somewhere else at the time. Nobody here holds it against you. Nobody here would say so if they did.
That it keeps wizards. We keep goats. Each to their own.

topics.text: Is there anything to drink in this village?
lines: The brewer's hut, when the wheat comes in. Until then there is water, and the water is good, and nobody here will admit it.

empire.note: Imperial: measured, courteous, roads and ledgers. Blue.
intro_home: {name}, {trade}, at the service of the settlement and, I suppose, of its apprentice. What may I tell you?
intro_away: {name}, {trade} of {this_village}. You will be the apprentice from {home_village}; your name arrived before you did, on a cart. State your business, and welcome.
Good day. {name}, {trade}. {this_village} does not often see a staff from {home_village} on its roads. We keep good roads; do use them.
hub: Yes? I am at your disposal, briefly.
What is it this time? I ask without rancour.
often: You have spoken to me more often than my own foreman. I note it without complaint.
Once more, then. I have begun to look forward to it, against my judgement.

lines: {this_village} is run properly: a ledger for every ware, a road for every ledger. We are {home_distance} tiles from your village and, in our own estimation, several centuries ahead of it.
That it has a wizard problem, and that the problem is young. Forgive me. We read the carriers' reports here and the carriers are not kind.
A stranger, a death in the square, an apprentice. It was in the dispatches. The dispatches did not say whose fault it was, which is how one knows it was somebody's.

topics.text: Why are your roads so straight?
lines: Because a crooked road is a slow road, and a slow road is a cold winter. We measured. Your village did not. One can tell from the air.

frisians.note: Frisian: terse, weather-bound, peat and dykes. Green.
intro_away: {name}. {trade}, {this_village}. From {home_village}, are you. Long way for a staff to walk. Ask what you came to ask.
The apprentice. {name}, {trade}. News walks faster than you do; we had it yesterday. Well?
often: Again. The peat does not cut itself, but go on.
You have more questions than the sea has water. Ask one.

lines: {this_village}: peat, dyke, wind, repeat. We hold the ground the water wants. It is enough to be going on with.
That a stranger came, and a wizard died, and the apprentice lived. Here we would have said: the water took one. It means the same.
Not much. Your village is dry country; dry country has dry troubles. Ours drown.
Coming. It is always coming. Ask me what it is doing when it arrives.

atlanteans.note: Atlantean: formal, curious, the sea and the old craft. Yellow.
intro_home: {name}, {trade}. The settlement greets its apprentice. What would you know?
intro_away: {name}, {trade} of {this_village}. An apprentice of {home_village}, so far from your own water. We have heard. Speak; we listen more carefully than the others.
Welcome, apprentice of {home_village}. I am {name}, {trade}. Our village remembers the old craft better than most; it will be interested in you.
hub: Another question. Good. Questions are how the craft survives.
often: You return to the same well. The well does not mind.
Again. I have begun to think you are studying me. It is permitted.

lines: {this_village} was built by people who remembered the sea and did not trust it. Every wall faces the water. Every ledger is kept twice. We are patient, and we are {home_distance} tiles from the nearest wizard, which is as patience likes it.
That the old craft is alive there in one old teacher and one young apprentice, and that the teacher is now dead. We mourned him here, briefly, in the old way. You would not have known.
That the Trial gate stands near it, {gate_distance} tiles or so {gate_compass} of here as the road goes, and that the apprentice has not yet gone in. We notice such things.

topics.text: You say 'the old craft'. What do you mean?
lines: The weave you carry in that staff. Our grandmothers wove it from six colours and four places, before the schools cut it down to three. The valley is remembering; have you not felt it?

amazons.note: Amazon: direct, forest-wise, hunters and trees. Purple.
intro_home: {name}, {trade}. Walk quietly; the forest is listening. What do you want?
intro_away: {name}, {trade} of {this_village}. You walk like someone from {home_village}: loud. Say what you came to say.
The staff from {home_village}. {name}, {trade}. The trees told us before the carriers did. Ask.
often: Five times. The forest has stopped falling silent when you come; take it as a compliment.
Again. Sit, then, if you are staying.

lines: {this_village} does not clear the forest; it moves through it. Hunters, gatherers, a few who plant. You will not find a quarry here and you will not find a fool.
That it burns its trees for lessons. The lumberjacks' tale, perhaps. Perhaps not.
That a stranger killed your teacher in the open, in daylight, and walked away. Here he would not have reached the square. Here nobody reaches the square.

topics.text: Why do you live under the trees?
lines: Because the trees were here first and will be here last. Everything you build in the open, the open takes back. Ask your warehouse keeper about rats.
